label: D2 step after choosing a1 (weakly after a2 late in the episode)
explanation: Fires only at D2 (DELAY_2), never at D1 and essentially never at GO. Within D2 it fires on 100% of trials where the agent chose a1 (in_action == 1, observed at D2), with large magnitude (top windows all a1, ~0.85-1.0 of max, slightly higher for common S1 than rare S2). After an a2 choice it fires only about half the time, mostly in the later part of the episode (ep_trial >= 60), and those activations are weak (mostly < 0.15 of max, the lowest quartile). Plain phase == D2 gives dev F1 0.86 with mass recall 1.0; adding the a1 / late-episode split raises F1 to 0.94 (precision 0.98, mass recall 0.98). Reward, transition type, stay/switch and the hidden good state add little once the choice is known. So it is mainly a D2 feature for the a1 choice, with a weak a2 component that grows over the episode. Uses only observed variables (the choice input at D2 and trial time).

issues: The magnitude claim is wrong. The explanation says a2 activations are weak (mostly below 0.15 of max), but a2 strength rises steadily with ep_trial. On dev, a2 at D2 with ep_trial >= 80 has precision 1.0, holds 18.7% of all activation mass, and makes up 28.6% of the top activation quartile. At ep_trial 90-99, a2 D2 activations fall almost entirely in the top quartile (top-quartile coverage 0.135 and 0.123, with no coverage in the lower quartiles). So the label's 'weakly after a2 late in the episode' is false for the last ~15 trials, where a2 steps are among the strongest activations.

The claim that a1 activations are strong (0.85-1.0 of max) comes only from late-episode top windows. a1 at D2 with ep_trial < 50 never reaches the top quartile (coverage 0.0). In the test misses windows, early-episode a1 D2 activations are about 0.28-0.46 of max. The top quartile is covered 100% by ep_trial >= 50, and plain (phase == D2) & (ep_trial >= 85) covers 63% of it whatever the choice.

A better reading is a graded code: D2 activation is roughly an a1 offset plus a ramp over trial-in-episode. The binary predicate is a threshold on that sum, so its 'a1 vs a2' framing hides the strong time dependence. The time effect is the main driver of the largest activations.

Most binary claims hold. D1 has 0 activity, GO has 19 of 380k steps, a1 at D2 is active 100% of the time, and a2 at D2 with ep_trial < 60 has precision 0.16-0.36 (weak, bottom quartile). Plain D2 scores F1 0.857. The missed activations (a2 early in the episode) are weak, holding 1.9% of mass on test. Part of them are switch trials: a2 with ep_trial < 60 and stay == 0 has precision 0.87. Adding stay == 0, which is observed at D2, raises test F1 from 0.933 to 0.944.
The test false positives are a2 D2 steps around ep_trial 60-65, where a2 precision is only 0.60. This is a soft threshold, consistent with a ramp.
skeptic.revised_label: D2 step only. Strength grows with trial-in-episode, with a boost after choosing a1: a1 D2 steps always fire (moderately early, strongly late), and a2 D2 steps fire from about trial 60 on, becoming among the strongest activations by trial 85-99.
